title: Adaptive safety policy tuner for canary metrics and shadow traffic
creator: James Park
description: Problem: Our current rollout guardrails rely on static thresholds (e.g. error_rate > 0.5% for 5m) which are brittle across workloads. This causes noisy rollbacks for traffic spikes, and slow detection for regressions in token cost or throughput. Goal: implement an adaptive safety policy tuner that derives rollback triggers from observed baselines and percentile-aware windows across latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput. The tuner must support canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes and be configurable per-customer/model.
acceptance_criteria: Canary deployments in staging with 2% traffic exposure trigger automatic rollback when multi-metric policy exceeds tuned thresholds in >= 3 independent backtests
Backtest harness runs against last 90 days of production traces and produces false-positive rate < 1% and true-positive detection of known incidents >= 90%
Operators can override or pin thresholds per rollout via Console; defaults arrive from the tuner and are visible in rollout UI
The system supports shadow traffic (no user-visible rollback) to validate policy updates with a no-impact mode
Telemetry includes per-rollback rationale: contributing metrics, window, and threshold values; visible in incident timeline
implementation_notes: Add new component: rollout-safety-tuner (service) that consumes metric streams and produces per-model policy suggestions
Use percentiles (P50/P95/P99) for latency and per-minute token cost distribution instead of simple means
Derive thresholds from baseline: threshold = baseline + max(alpha * stddev, min_delta). Parameters alpha/min_delta are tunable and recordable
Implement hysteresis and cool-down: require violation sustained for N consecutive windows and block rollbacks within cooldown period
Integrate with existing rollout engine via the policy API (extend /rollouts/:id/policy-suggestion endpoint)
Support a simulated evaluation path that can be run against historical traces stored in metric-archive (see experiment_plan)
experiment_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit tests + simulation harness. Validate tuner math with synthetic sequences (spikes, drift, step changes)
Phase 1 (shadow): deploy policy suggestions to canary teams as shadow decisions for 2 weeks. No automated rollbacks; collect precision/recall metrics
Phase 2 (limited-auto): enable auto-rollback for internal staging namespaces with stricter alpha and longer cool-down
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): enable for 10% of production rollouts, monitor for 2 weeks, then expand with safety knobs
Rollback backstop: always have an immediate manual rollback/abort path for on-call
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: per-rollout multi-metric view (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost per request, throughput RPS)
Alerts: alert when tuner suggests a threshold drift > 2x historical variance or when auto-rollback occurs
On-call steps: verify metric sources, confirm rollout scope, examine contributing metrics, decide to accept or revert tuner suggestion
Post-rollback RCA checklist: collect traces, compare model outputs (if available), run offline A/B on archived traffic
simulation_notes: We will reuse the model-rollout-sim harness (repo: github.com/redwood/inference-rollout-sim) and add scenarios: network spikes, model slowdown, token-cost regression
Historical trace set: last_90_days_v2 in metric-archive; anonymize request IDs before local replay
Evaluation metrics: precision, recall, time-to-detect, false-positive rate, cost-of-false-positive (user impact estimator)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Adaptive thresholds can overfit short-term noise if windowing is too small; mitigated via min_window and smoothing
Using percentiles reduces sensitivity to outliers but may mask subpopulation regressions; we keep both percentile and tail-count checks
Aggressive auto-rollback reduces customer exposure to regressions but increases risk of user-visible interruptions; default conservatism is required for external customers
Complex policies increase operator cognitive load; UI should surface concise rationale and a one-click revert
